messages:
ajohnson: quick heads-up — after the kernel-selector change merged in today, we see a regression for Mistral-8x7b long-chat workloads using sliding-window attention. p99 spiked ~70% on our perf runs

maria: ugh. is this specific to the sliding-window path or a more general kv/cache issue?

kevin: looks like an interaction: the new kernel prefers tiled matmuls which are great normally, but when the runtime slices requests for sliding-window the KV pointers misalign and we get cache misses. profiler shows many small memcpy/convert ops.

ajohnson: exact numbers from local profiling: baseline (old kernel) p50=21ms p99=48ms. new kernel p50=23ms p99=82ms for 1k-length tokens with rolling window and batch size=4. throughput drops ~28%.

sam: can you paste the flamegraph snippet? maybe kernel chooser picks non-kernel for qkv reorder?

kevin: pasted snippet below (trimmed):
```
flame: runtime_kernel_selector -> tiled_gemm::launch -> copy_kv_tile -> rope_rescale -> attention_mask_apply -> sliding_window_index_fixup
heavy: copy_kv_tile (24%)
heavy: rope_rescale (18%)
```

maria: rope_rescale at 18% is suspicious. we do a per-head RoPE scaling when max_position_embeddings < requested length, and the new tiled kernels expect contiguous kv layout. the pointer arithmetic for window wrap was safe before but now causes extra memops.

ajohnson: reproduction: run long-chat synthetic with config: model=mistral-8x7b, seq=1024, max_pos=2048 override, batch=4, sliding_window=512, rope_scale=0.5. passes through new selector.

sam: try forcing kernel back to the old dense_gemm for that test to confirm: set env KERNEL_FORCE=dense_gemm and re-run.

kevin: did that — forcing dense_gemm restores p99 to ~50ms. so bug is definitely in combination: tiled_gemm + sliding-window + rope scaling + kv sharding.

maria: hypothesis: tiled_gemm uses 128x64 tiles and assumes KV tile aligned on GPU page boundaries. sliding-window wrap introduces non-aligned tails that trigger slow path in copy_kv_tile. also our rope scaling currently does per-token floats -> quant conversion which isn't fused.

ajohnson: options: 1) short-term rollback of kernel-selector for Mistral-8x7b sliding-window profiles; 2) add runtime fast-path to align tail tiles (cheap memcpy pad) when sliding-window enabled; 3) fuse rope scaling into kernel (longer).

sam: also check batching heuristics: our chosen batcher groups by seq length but not by sliding-window stride. mixing e.g., stride=128 with stride=512 in same batch increases misalignment risk. we can add a batch-key: sliding_stride.

kevin: logging from a failing run for reference:
```
[INFO] request_id=... model=mistral-8x7b len=1024 stride=512 kernel=tiled_gemm
[WARN] copy_kv_tile: tail_unaligned=true pad_alloc=256 bytes
[DEBUG] rope_rescale: applied scaling factor=0.5 per_head=true
[PERF] memcpy_us=1234 kernel_launch_us=945
```

maria: action items: kevin to prototype pad-fix (align tail tiles) and microbenchmark; sam to update batcher to split by sliding_stride and max_pos override; ajohnson to roll a canary with kernel-selector pinned for affected workload and gate the new selector until we have fix.

kevin: starting pad-fix now. initial microbench shows memset overhead <0.5% for aligned hits, but fixes the memcpy spikes on tails. will push patch to a feature branch.

sam: I'll add a lightweight metric emit when we mix different sliding_stride values into same batch so sigma can alert.

ajohnson: timeline: aim to canary pin by EOW if no blockers. kevin, if pad-fix looks stable we can instead opt to keep selector but require a sliding-window compatibility check in the chooser.

maria: note for follow-up: double-check max_position_embeddings override interaction. we had an edge where rope table resize + per-head kv dims (8x7b uses narrower kv head) produced wrong scaling indices for positions > model.max_pos. ensure we clamp before computing RoPE factors.

kevin: noted — will add a unit test for rope scaling vs. max_pos boundary and for head/kv dim combos.

ajohnson: thanks all. if anyone sees user-facing regressions ping #incidents and mark the canary build.

dev-bot: deploybot: scheduled canary roll (kernel-selector pin) -> eng-runtime-canary at 2026-03-19T02:00Z :rocket:
